newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Nortel in six mln ADS offer.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Nortel in six mln ADS offer.

text.p: Argentina's Nortel Inversora SA, a holding company for Telecom Argentina, Tuesday announced a secondary offering of six million American Depositary Shares (ADS) at $28.8 each.
Each ADS represents one-twentieth of a Series B Preferred Share of Nortel and will be listed in the New York Stock Exchange, Nortel said in a press release.
The secondary offering is made by unspecified holders of Series B Preferred Shares of Nortel.

The selling shareholders, most of whom were founding investors in Nortel in 1990, have also granted underwriters an option to purchase an additional 900,000 ADS to cover over-allotments if any, Nortel said.
Sales will be made on a pro rata basis.
Nortel will not receive any proceeds from the offering.

The Series B Preferred Shares are non-voting except in certain limited circumstances and can be redeemed at the option of the holders in the case of certain changes of control of Nortel, Nortel said. Otherwise they are basically equivalent to Nortel's common stock.
The managers of the offering are J.P. Morgan Securities Inc, Credit Suisse First Boston Corp (CSFB), Lehman Brothers and Credit Lyonnais Securities (USA) Inc .
Nortel owns 60 percent of the common stock of Telecom Argentina, which provides telecommunications services in northern Argentina.
Nortel is formed by Italy's STET (32.5 percent), France Telecom unit France Cable et Radio (32.5 percent), Argentine conglomerate Perez Companc (25 percent) and J.P. Morgan (10 percent).
